title: A help question sent again after a lost answer reaches MettleUp twice and is paid twice
what: In Help and feedback, the question is saved on MettleUp's side before the AI answers. If the answer is slow or lost, the app sends the same question again to the backup address by itself, and when the member then sees 'Couldn't send' and taps Send again, a brand-new question goes out. Each copy is saved, answered by the AI from the gym's credits, and listed again in Your questions (one failed, one answered).
expected: A question sent again after a lost answer is recognised as the same question and answered once.
fix_line: Give each question one id that survives a resend, and let the help box ignore a copy it already has

title: When MettleUp's help box is down, the member is told to check their own internet
what: If both MettleUp help addresses answer with a server fault, the member app shows the same words as having no internet: 'Couldn't send. Check your internet and try again.' The member's internet is fine, so they keep retrying or give up. The voice recording path already tells these two apart.
expected: A MettleUp server fault says MettleUp is having a problem and to try later; only a real lost connection asks the member to check their internet.
fix_line: Show separate words for a server fault, as the voice path does

title: A 'Did this solve it?' tap made with no internet never reaches MettleUp
what: After an AI answer, the member taps Yes or No. The tap is kept on the phone and the buttons show it as done, but it is sent once only. With no internet or a slow line it is dropped with a phone-only log line and never sent again. MettleUp's count of how often the AI help works misses those taps.
expected: A tap that could not be sent is sent again later, or the member sees it did not go through.
fix_line: Keep unsent ratings and send them with the next help check

title: Crash reports miss crashes on the Android side and any crash on a phone with no internet
what: The member app's crash reports catch only errors in its own screen code. A crash inside the Android parts of the app (the native pieces, out of memory, a frozen app) is not reported at all, so copies installed from GitHub, which Google Play's crash list does not see, report nothing. A crash report is also sent once, at the moment of the crash, with no copy kept: a crash in a gym basement with no signal, or one that closes the app before the 1.5 second wait ends, is lost for good.
expected: Every crash kind, including Android-side ones, reaches MettleUp, and a report that could not be sent waits on the phone for the next launch.
how_often: whenever the app crashes offline or on the Android side
fix_line: Keep unsent crash reports on the phone and send them next launch; add a catcher for the Android side

title: A crash that comes back after a fix, or spreads to many phones, raises no new alert
what: The daily crash check opens one GitHub issue per new crash kind. A kind that already has an issue, open or closed, never gets anything new: a crash fixed and closed that returns in a later version, or one that grows from 1 phone to 500, stays silent. The check also ends green, with only a notice, when its reading key is not set or the crash list is not private, so the alerts can be off without anyone being told.
expected: A closed crash kind that appears again reopens its issue, a fast-growing kind is flagged, and a switched-off check fails loudly.
fix_line: Reopen or comment on a known crash kind when it shows up again or its count jumps; fail the run when the check is off

title: The member app measures nothing: no sign-up, first-workout, day-30 or free-month-to-Plus numbers
what: The member app sends no usage numbers at all: no count of installs, first workout logged, members still training on day 30, or how many finish the free month and buy MettleUp Plus. The free month starts and ends on the phone, and purchases are known only to the phone. Plus pricing, the free-month length and the member growth plan are decided blind, though MettleUp is judged on members still training on day 30.
expected: A small set of private, no-personal-data counts (first workout, still active on day 30, free month ended, Plus bought) reaches MettleUp.
fix_line: Add a few anonymous milestone counts and show them in HQ
